decisions.decision: Which rulings does this plan inherit from plan 1?
decisions.ruling: Keep the yml/ namespace (plan 1 D2). Credit the MIT code in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md plus a one-line source header in each ported file, test files included (plan 1 D5). Put the code in src/plugins/yml/ inside this package (plan 1 D7).
decisions.rejected: A new namespace; a separate package

decisions.decision: Which packages are kept and which are ported?
decisions.ruling: The user's criterion: a direct dependency is not a concern; the problem is transitive dependencies that conflict between direct dependencies. Port eslint-plugin-yml (peer eslint >=9.38.0, its own ranges on @eslint/core and @eslint/plugin-kit). Keep yaml-eslint-parser (transitives yaml, which we pin, and eslint-visitor-keys ^5, which ESLint pins as ^5.0.1; no peers). Add @eslint/plugin-kit, @ota-meshi/ast-token-store, natural-compare, diff-sequences and escape-string-regexp as direct, exact-pinned, bundled dependencies (no peers; transitives none or already pinned by ESLint).
decisions.rejected: Port yaml-eslint-parser; port the small packages

decisions.decision: Which yml rules do we port?
decisions.ruling: All 30 rules of eslint-plugin-yml 3.10.0 except the Vue-only rule vue-custom-block/no-parsing-error (D12).
decisions.rejected: Only the 7 enabled rules; the 16 non-layout rules; all 31

decisions.decision: Do we port the YAML language?
decisions.ruling: Yes: upstream src/language/ (YAMLLanguage and YAMLSourceCode) becomes src/plugins/yml/language/. The plugin registers it as languages.yaml, so the language name stays yml/yaml.
decisions.rejected: Keep eslint-plugin-yml for its language

decisions.decision: What test bar do the rules and the language meet?
decisions.ruling: A RuleTester test for each rule, ported from the upstream test at tag v3.10.0 with the upstream config (plugins { yml: our plugin }, language yml/yaml) and the upstream fixture loader; plus the upstream language tests and the casing utils test, as D13 c and D14 limit them. The golden snapshots must keep the same problems and fixes.
decisions.rejected: Golden snapshots only

decisions.decision: How do we port the upstream fixtures?
decisions.ruling: Copy upstream tests/fixtures/rules/ at tag v3.10.0 to tests/unit/plugins/yml/fixtures/rules/, except the .vue files and their sidecars (D10, D15 c) and tests/fixtures/rules/vue-custom-block/ (D12); yaml-test-suite/ and integrations/ are not copied (D14, D15 b). Port the upstream loader (tests/utils/utils.ts without makeSuiteTests, and apply-fixer.ts) to tests/unit/plugins/yml/helpers/. Widen the pre-commit exclude from ^tests/fixtures/ to ^tests/(.*/)?fixtures/ in .config/pre-commit-config.yaml and in .config/bootstrap/tools.toml (D15 a).
decisions.rejected: Inline cases only; fetch the fixtures at test time

decisions.decision: Where does the rule configuration live?
decisions.ruling: In the yaml preset, as in plan 1 D13. The plugin index (written by U5) exports meta, rules (merged from rules/group-a.ts, group-b.ts, group-c.ts) and languages { yaml }. No configs. The preset reproduces the flat/recommended config of eslint-plugin-yml exactly (language, the yml/ rule severities and options, and the core rules it turns off), except that it does not set yml/vue-custom-block/no-parsing-error (D12), and it keeps files ["**/*.yaml", "**/*.yml"] (D13).
decisions.rejected: configs inside our plugin

decisions.decision: How is parity proved?
decisions.ruling: After U5, lint/problems.json and lint/fixes.json of the golden tests do not change. The config snapshots of file.yaml and file.yml can change only in their parser field and by the removal of the yml/vue-custom-block/no-parsing-error entry. Any other golden change stops the run with a QUESTION.
decisions.rejected: Accept any golden change

decisions.decision: Review unit and execution mode
decisions.ruling: One review unit after U5, because the change ships runnable code. Execution mode teams, because wave 2 has three edit units; if a team cannot start, the run uses solo.
decisions.rejected: Wave review only; solo

decisions.decision: How do we treat the 37 .vue fixtures?
decisions.ruling: Skip them: do not copy the .vue fixture files, and drop the vue-eslint-parser branch of the loader. This linter has no Vue preset, and the user never uses Vue.
decisions.rejected: Add vue-eslint-parser as an exact-pinned devDependency

decisions.decision: Release level
decisions.ruling: MINOR: the Vue-only rule yml/vue-custom-block/no-parsing-error is removed (a scan of ~/Projects on 2026-11-22 found no consumer .config/linter.yaml that names it); the other 30 rules, the language name and the behavior stay the same.
decisions.rejected: PATCH; MAJOR

decisions.decision: Do we port the Vue-only rule vue-custom-block/no-parsing-error?
decisions.ruling: No. The user never uses Vue: a scan of ~/Projects on 2026-11-22 found .vue files only in a third-party clone (tmp/mise), no Vue dependency in any package.json, and no Vue rule in any of the 25 .config/linter.yaml files. Do not port the rule, its tests or its fixtures (upstream tests/fixtures/rules/vue-custom-block/). A YAML syntax error is still a fatal parse error of the language. Plan 1 drops tailwindcss/require-reference-in-vue by the same ruling.
decisions.rejected: Keep and port it

decisions.decision: Round 1 rulings review: how do the ported files fit wave order, types and tooling?
decisions.ruling: (a) U1 does not port upstream src/utils/rules.ts; the group registries and the plugin index replace it. (b) The ported loadTestCases takes the plugin object as a parameter; it imports no plugin index. (c) The upstream test yaml-source-code-with-stylistic-rules is not ported: it needs @stylistic/eslint-plugin, a new third-party plugin. (d) natural-compare ships no types: U1 writes src/plugins/yml/natural-compare.d.ts with a local declare module; no @types package. The ported code takes JSON-schema types from @eslint/core (for example RulesMeta["schema"]), never from json-schema. (e) U5 owns src/cli/commands/version.ts and keeps @eslint/plugin-kit out of the --version plugin list, which lists plugins only. (f) The preset keeps files ["**/*.yaml", "**/*.yml"], the same set as upstream, since **/ also matches the root. (g) The ported loader never writes a fixture: a missing errors.json or output file fails the test.
decisions.rejected: Port utils/rules.ts; a lazy import of the plugin index; add @stylistic/eslint-plugin; add @types/natural-compare; print @eslint/plugin-kit in --version; copy the upstream files list; keep the fixture write path

decisions.decision: Round 2 rulings review: which upstream tests and fixtures are ported?
decisions.ruling: (a) U1 does not port tests/src/language/directive-comments.ts, because each of its 20 cases needs yml/no-empty-key; U5 ports it whole into tests/unit/plugins/yml/language/with-rules.test.ts. (b) makeSuiteTests of tests/utils/utils.ts is dropped: it only writes fixtures, and no test calls it. (c) U1 ports tests/src/utils/casing.ts to tests/unit/plugins/yml/language/casing.test.ts. (d) The tests of src/utils/rules.ts, src/meta.ts, tests/src/eslint-plugin.ts and tests/src/configs/ are not ported: we port no rules.ts, no upstream meta and no configs. (e) So U1 copies only tests/fixtures/rules/ (D15 b).
decisions.rejected: Port every upstream test file; copy all fixture directories

decisions.decision: Round 3 rulings review: the bootstrap exclude, the dead suite fixtures and the .vue sidecars
decisions.ruling: (a) U1 also owns .config/bootstrap/tools.toml and widens [tools.pre-commit] exclude from ^tests/fixtures/ to ^tests/(.*/)?fixtures/, the same value as in .config/pre-commit-config.yaml, so that a bootstrap sync keeps it. (b) U1 copies only upstream tests/fixtures/rules/; yaml-test-suite/ is read only by the dropped makeSuiteTests. (c) U1 skips the sidecar files of each .vue fixture: for an input <dir>/<stem>-input.vue, every <dir>/<stem>-* file.
decisions.rejected: Accept the drift with bootstrap; copy yaml-test-suite/; copy the orphan sidecars

decisions.decision: Round 4: the sort-keys case that lints the upstream package.json
decisions.ruling: U1 copies the upstream package.json at tag v3.10.0, byte for byte, to tests/unit/plugins/yml/fixtures/upstream-package.json. The ported sort-keys test lints that copy with OPTIONS_FOR_PACKAGE_JSON, in place of ../../../package.json.
decisions.rejected: Lint this repo package.json; drop the case

decisions.decision: Round 4: who formats the files before the check-only unit gate?
decisions.ruling: Each edit unit runs mise x -- mise run code:format --fix before it returns, so that the unit gate (code:format, check only) passes. test:golden --update stays as written: the task passes a part flag with no --.
decisions.rejected: A --fix unit gate

decisions.decision: What does a unit do when a ported upstream test fails only because ESLint 10 or vitest is stricter? (ruled by the user on 2026-11-22 for all B08 plans)
decisions.ruling: A ported upstream test case that fails only because ESLint 10's RuleTester or the vitest wiring is stricter than upstream's setup (jest on ESLint 9) — not because the rule behaves differently — may have its test setup changed: for example, remove a duplicate case, or add a property that ESLint 10 requires. Never change the expected messages, message ids, locations, output or suggestions. List each change as DECIDED; the review unit checks them. A case whose expected result differs stops the run with a QUESTION.
decisions.rejected: Stop and ask for each case; apply it to one plan only

decisions.decision: How are eslint-disable comments for unknown rules and strict-TypeScript errors in ported code handled?
decisions.ruling: (a) A ported file may drop an eslint-disable or eslint-enable comment that names a rule this repo does not define, or rewrite it to the rule of this repo that it means; ESLint 10 reports an unknown rule in such a comment as an error, so code:lint would fail. (b) Where the repo's strict TypeScript (noUncheckedIndexedAccess, verbatimModuleSyntax, .js import extensions) rejects ported code, a unit fixes it only with changes that have no runtime effect: non-null assertions, casts, type annotations, import type, and .js or /index.js on relative imports. No runtime guard is added. List each kind of change as DECIDED. (Ruled for all B08 plans on 2026-11-22, from the rulings review of plan 6.)
decisions.rejected: Define the unknown rules; add runtime guards

decisions.decision: Q1: Does ruling D19 (b) also allow the TypeScript override keyword, which noImplicitOverride requires on a ported subclass method (YAMLSourceCode.traverse)?
decisions.ruling: Allow override under D19 (b) for all B08 plans — U1 stays as written, and later language ports may use it too.
decisions.rejected: Keep D19 (b) closed — the port needs a tsconfig change or another ruling

decisions.decision: Q2: How is the self-lint error no-useless-assignment at src/plugins/yml/rules/flow-sequence-bracket-newline.ts:82 (ported upstream `let minItems = 0;`) cleared?
decisions.ruling: Add `// eslint-disable-next-line no-useless-assignment -- ported upstream code` above the line — the code stays identical to upstream.
decisions.rejected: Change it to `let minItems: number;`; Leave it and keep code:lint red

decisions.decision: Q3: How is the max-len fixture test fixed when tests/unit/plugins/yml/fixtures/rules/max-len/invalid/ does not exist (its only upstream fixture was .vue)?
decisions.ruling: Change the U1 loader to treat a missing valid/ or invalid/ directory as empty — a setup-only fix in a U1-owned file, made by a re-dispatched U1.
decisions.rejected: Change max-len.test.ts under D18 to run only valid/; Add a placeholder .gitkeep

decisions.decision: Q4: How are the 3 sort-keys 2XXW output-test failures fixed, caused by the U1 loader filtering skipOutputTest inside a describe callback that vitest defers past the delete?
decisions.ruling: Fix the U1 loader so the filtered list is computed before the describe — a setup-only fix in a U1-owned file, made by a re-dispatched U1.
decisions.rejected: Pass { skipOutputTest: true } in sort-keys.test.ts; Leave the 3 failures

decisions.decision: Q5: Should ported yml rule tests keep upstream `new RuleTester({})` where upstream has it, or always pass { plugins: { yml: plugin }, language: "yml/yaml" }?
decisions.ruling: Keep upstream `new RuleTester({})` where upstream has it, and U2 reverts its 9 constructors — the port stays a line-for-line copy of upstream, and the three groups match.
decisions.rejected: Always pass plugins and language; U3 and U4 change their 6 constructors
